title: FAVLA: A Force-Adaptive Fast-Slow VLA model for Contact-Rich Robotic Manipulation
affiliations: USTC 等 (Yanyong Zhang / Jianmin Ji 组，据作者推断)
abstract: Force/torque feedback can substantially improve VLA models on contact-rich manipulation, but most existing approaches fuse all modalities at a single operating frequency, ignoring mismatched sensor sampling rates and forcing downsampling of high-frequency contact cues. FAVLA is a force-adaptive fast-slow VLA that decouples slow perception planning from fast contact-aware control: a slow VLM runs at fixed low frequency to encode modalities and predict near-future force variation, while a fast action expert executes at a variable high frequency conditioned on the latest force. A force adapter injects high-frequency force features into multiple AE layers, and AE execution frequency is adaptively scheduled by the predicted force variation.
